# AI Acknowledgement

One of the use cases for the skills map is to help students to identify how to articulate how they have used GenAI in coursework. Acknowledgements can be developed along discipline guidelines, or along institutional guidelines. Below we have examples of both.

Most journals expect the use of GenAI to be acknowledged and there is a difference between citing GenAI as a source and acknowledging it as a tool. As the output of GenAI is not stable or repeatable, it cannot be used as a source since a reader will not be able to access the source themselves. Acknowledgement as a tool is done in two ways. The first is within the text, such as a methods section of a report, where an author describes how they used the tool for specific tasks. The second is a more general acknowledgement in a dedicated section. The [Consortia Advancing Standards in Research Administration Information](https://casrai.org/guides/ai-disclosure-statement-examples) provides a summary of different journal expectations and provides example forms of wording. The their [additional guidance(APA)](https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/resources/publishing-tips/policy-generative-ai) the American Psychological Association provides a guide to disclosing AI situated within a range of existing guidance.

Best practice in acknowledgements for assessed work is to include them as an appendix or as an author note at the end of the text (before reference).

## Discipline-specific example

The first example is student-facing advice based on the APA guidelines above.

When you engage in putting together ideas in order to answer a question in an assessment, you are practising synthesis. This can be done through thinking and manipulating the knowledge that you have already accumulated. Alternatively it can be done by using resources from elsewhere or through brainstorming with the us of an GenAI.

When doing the task yourself, you would develop a research question and use that to organise the literature and knowledge you already have to answer the questions. In doing so, you develop an argument to answer the question. As you answer, you would refer back to your literature to verify and cite the evidence that supports your argument.

However, people often have gaps in their knowledge and in that case they refer to the arguments that others have made or use tools to help them find the evidence to support their arguments. The table below gives and example of how you would cite various sources of evidence. It is based on a task where students are asked write a short forum post for their peers.

While this shows a safe way to use GenAI, we strongly recommend that you try th tasks without the use of AI first. Every argument that you constructy yourself, every time you manipulate your knowledge in a new way and every time you gain new knowledge with a scaffold (or research question) that you made yourself, you are deepening your understanding and building specialised skills and knowledge for your subject.

## Appendix with ticked items

Below is an example of a tick-box declaration of AI use. Students are fist asked if they take take responsibility for their work and are then prompted to pick different ways that they uses AI. You can use the skills map to generate an assessment-specific or dicipline-specific list of items.

This can also be developed as a survey activity on an learning management system such as Moodle. For instance teachers can make it conditional on the assessment that a student first had to complete the declaration of AI use before they were allowed submit.

**Appendix A**

Generative AI Declaration

Please add this after your references. It is not included in the wordcount.

Tick any relevant boxes to indicate how you have used generative AI tools in your assignment.

You MUST declare all use of AI and take responsibility for the content of the assignment. We consider it a misuse of generative AI if you do not declare all uses.

**Question 1.** Do you take full responsibility for the content of this submission, ensuring its adherence to academic integrity standards and compliance with University and subject-specific regulations regarding generative AI use as detailed in the assessment information sheet?

- [ ] Tick the box if you take full responsibility for the content of this submission.

**Question 2.** Select all that apply to you for this assessment:

- [ ] Idea generation or scoping of topic or research question\
- [ ] Outlining or structuring sections of the work\
- [ ] Language editing for spelling, grammar, clarity or tone\
- [ ] Translation of my own text in another language into English\
- [ ] Rephrasing my own text at sentence level\
- [ ] Summarising or explaining primary sources like journal articles\
- [ ] Suggesting search terms or potential sources for me to review\
- [ ] Referencing support, for example checking or producing citations, DOIs or formatting\
- [ ] Analysis support, for example statistical advice or interpreting output\
- [ ] Coding assistance, for example writing or debugging code\
- [ ] Visuals or media support, for example producing figures, diagrams, slide layout or transcription of my own recordings\
- [ ] I did not use Generative AI tools in any way to assist with this assignment or my learning of the topic\
- [ ] Other (describe below)

**Question 3.** Please share if/how you used Generative AI in a way other than those listed above, or if there is anything else you would like to share regarding this assessment and Generative AI.
